title: Debt Elimination Strategies: Avalanche vs Snowball
content:
High-interest consumer debt, particularly from credit cards and personal loans, is one of the most formidable barriers to building long-term wealth. When carrying debt with 20%+ annual percentage rates (APR), guaranteed interest charges erase any returns an investor could realistically expect in the stock market.

Two structured debt payoff methodologies have demonstrated proven success: the Debt Avalanche method and the Debt Snowball method.

The Debt Avalanche method prioritizes mathematically optimal debt elimination. Under this strategy, the debtor pays the minimum required on all debts, and channels all remaining surplus cash toward the single debt with the highest interest rate. Once that highest-interest balance is extinguished, the cash flow rolls down to the next highest rate. This minimizes the total dollar amount paid in interest over time and accelerates debt freedom.

The Debt Snowball method, popularized by Dave Ramsey, prioritizes behavioral psychology over pure mathematics. In this approach, debts are listed in order of smallest balance to largest balance, regardless of interest rates. By aggressively paying off the smallest balance first, the debtor scores quick psychological wins, generating momentum and motivation to sustain the payoff journey.

Both methods work because they enforce intentional focus. As a general rule, debt with interest rates exceeding 7-8% should be eliminated aggressively before investing surplus funds beyond the 401(k) employer match.
